name: idle-vivarium-ferns-day-b
refs: IMAGE 1, THE AUTHORITY (room 1's signed painting by day): the device, the camera, the lens, the scale, the finish and the light. Never the layout of its planting; none of its floor dressing (roots, succulents, stones, seep) appears:

IMAGE 2, THE LAYOUT MAP (structure and placement only, never the look), a diagram; nothing of it is painted: the dark grey is the back zone where the tall planting stands; the light grey is the open floor; where they meet is the floor's back edge:
IMAGE 3, SUBJECT AND MATERIAL ONLY (leaf litter and forest-floor ground): never its finish, never its tree trunks:
prompt: Output a NEW image, 16:9. The SAME terrarium inside the SAME rugged field device as Image 1, seen from the same eye height with the same lens and the same depth of field: the left wall with its braided feed line and connector, the right wall with its mister arm and slatted vent, the dark soil strip along the foot, each exactly where it is in Image 1. Inside it a NEW planting, painted in the Miniature Lives finish of Image 1: fine grain on the world, soft bokeh behind, a warm key light from the top left with its shafts. Cute by craft, never childish: no cartoon outlines, no toy colours, no gloss, no glow, no chrome, no alien tech. No creatures, no animals, no figures, no text, no letters, no digits, no logos, no frame, no UI. No water except one small flat seep. Pebbles and leaves at the scale of Image 1's. THE NEW PLANTING: a fern bank of broad fronds fanning out across the back (from about 29 to 74 percent of the width, rising to about 28 percent of the height from the top): deep green fronds with lighter new fronds and curled croziers. A fallen log, mossy and soft-barked, lies along the back edge of the floor from about 14 to 55 percent of the width, its top at about 58 percent of the height and its underside resting ON the back edge, fronds growing over it; it never crosses onto the floor. The floor: leaf litter lying flat in warm browns, moss, a few small croziers, two small fern tufts at most; their feet end at the back edge; nothing on the floor larger than a small pebble except two pieces no larger than a fist. No tree trunks, no forest: it is a terrarium planting. Fern greens warm, never cooler than Image 1's moss. Do NOT copy Image 1's burrow, root mound, succulents or its pool: Image 1 is the authority on the device, camera, scale, finish and light only. THE OPEN FLOOR (the light grey of Image 2, from its boundary with the dark grey down to the dark soil strip) is low open ground, the open floor sunlit as brightly as Image 1's floor, nothing a small creature could perch on: every piece on it lower than a pebble-and-a-half (about 32 px of a 568 px tall picture), at most two rounded or leafy pieces up to about twice that, never flat-topped; no flat raised top, no ledge, no slab, no step; no log, root or stem lying across the floor; everything tall stands BEHIND the back edge, its feet ending on it, never spilling forward onto the floor. The back edge of the floor (where open floor ends and the planting behind begins) runs along the boundary between the dark grey and the light grey of Image 2, or a little above it (never more than about 24 px), never below it. The device walls at the left and the right hold only the wall, the feed line and its connector at the left, the mister and the vent at the right, kept clear of planting.
